chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Abī Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about sea water: Is it purifying? He said: “Yes.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Flowing water is not rendered najis by anything that falls into it from creatures possessing flowing blood and dies in it, nor by any najasah, unless it overcomes the water and changes its color, taste, or smell. That only occurs with a small amount of water, weak flow, and a large amount of najasah. All that has preceded from the verse and the reports indicates this, and that the name of water applies to it. As for that which indicates that when it changes, its use is not permissible.

key_terms.أَطَهُورٌ: whether it is purifying and suitable for ritual purification
key_terms.فَيُغَيِّرَ لَوْنَهُ أَوْ طَعْمَهُ أَوْ: changes its color, taste, or smell

ai.seo_question: Is sea water purifying, and when does flowing water become najis in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that sea water is tahir and purifying, and the accompanying legal discussion explains that flowing water is not made najis by contact with najasah unless its color, taste, or smell is altered. The passage is significant in Shia fiqh for establishing rulings on taharah and the legal status of natural and flowing waters.
